request.query: Migri Temporary protection Helsinki, Finland tips, what to bring, what I forgot, problems
request.objective: First-hand experiences and newcomer guides about "Temporary protection" (Migri) in Helsinki, Finland: practical tricks, documents people forgot or were unexpectedly asked for, and things that went wrong.

results.title: Temporary Protection in Finland 2026 | ENB Consulting
results.author: Erkan Bayar
highlights:
Temporary protection for people who fled the war in Ukraine has been extended to 4 March 2028, while the residence permits granted on that basis are valid until 4 March 2027. Since 5 August 2026 a permit on the basis of temporary protection can be granted only to Ukrainian citizens who are authorised to leave Ukraine. The application is registered with the police or the border authority on arrival, and the right to work and study begins at that registration; the right to work is not limited to any field. After a year of living in Finland you can apply to DVV for a municipality of residence, and earlier if you were granted a temporary protection permit for at least a year or if a family member already has one. Migri advises anyone with a job or a study place to apply for a different residence permit. A temporary protection permit ends by itself on 12 August 2026 if another permit granted before 12 June 2026 is still valid that day, and at once if another permit is granted on or after 12 June 2026.

...

What matters in practice is to watch the expiry date on your own permit card separately.

...

An application for temporary protection is registered with the police or the border authority on arrival in Finland. Migri's current estimate is that a complete application is processed in about a week; the decision then takes roughly another week to arrive by post, so it usually reaches you within two weeks.

The residence permit card is produced separately. Migri says the card takes about two weeks and is sent to a collection point within three weeks of the decision. These are estimates: a missing document or a request for further information lengthens them.

...

Under temporary protection the right to work and study does not wait for the decision: it begins when the application is registered with the police or the border authority. That is the most practical difference between this route and the ordinary residence permit routes.

The right to work carries no restriction by field. Migri's guidance to employers is explicit: an employee who has applied for temporary protection has an unrestricted right to work and may take a job in any field. The employer still has to see the basis of that right and meet the ordinary employer obligations.

...

## 7. Common mistakes

### Checklist

- Taking the arrangement's 2028 date for the expiry date on your own permit card
- Assuming the right to work does not start until the decision arrives
- Asking Migri for a municipality of residence, when the application goes to DVV
- Waiting out the year without checking the exceptions to the one-year rule
- Assuming temporary protection continues after another permit is granted
- Not reporting a change of address and risking the card reaching the collection point

## 8. Temporary protection checklist

### Checklist

- Has the application been registered with the police or the border authority?
- Has the position been checked against the 5 August 2026 rule?
- Does the family tie date from before 24 February 2022?
- Has the expiry date on your own permit card been noted separately?
- Has the employer been told that the right to work starts at registration?
- Has the municipality of residence application been planned against the one-year rule or its exceptions?
- If there is a job or a study place, has another permit route been assessed?
- Has the date on which temporary protection will end after a new permit been worked out?
- Are the address and contact details up to date?

results.title: Finnish Police: When to Contact Them and What Documents to Prepare | International Law Firm "Zahist"
results.author: Anna Müller
highlights:
| --- | --- |
| Crime report | Passport, permit card, description of the event, evidence |

...

| Passport or identity card | Passport or permit card, photograph meeting police requirements |
| Advice on licences | Passport and an appointment booking, if required |

...

## Temporary protection and the police: what Ukrainians need to know

Applications for temporary protection are submitted to the police or the border guard. They register the application and record personal data, place of residence and family details. The applicant also provides a photograph, fingerprints and a signature. The decision is made by Migri. Filing the application is free of charge, and the right to work arises immediately after registration. After that, all questions concerning status are handled by Migri, not the police. Therefore, for a permit card, an extension or changes, contact Migri through Enter Finland, as we explained in the article on losing a card.

...

## How to prepare for a visit to a police station

Good preparation shortens the appointment and reduces the risk of mistakes. Decide the purpose of your visit in advance and check whether an appointment is required.

1. Define the purpose of the visit: a report, lost documents, or a licence service.
2. Check whether a prior appointment is required.
3. Gather identity documents and evidence of the event.
4. Write down a chronology of events with dates and times.
5. Prepare contact details and a telephone number at which you can be reached.
6. If an interpreter is needed, say so at the start of the conversation.

During the conversation, speak calmly and only about facts you know. Do not guess or invent details, as this may harm your case. Ask for confirmation that the report has been filed and keep it.

...

Contacting the police does not in itself change your status, but incorrect information may create problems. If you file a report as a victim, your permit is not cancelled merely because you contacted the police. However, any decision must be assessed in the context of your case.

| Situation | What to pay attention to |
| --- | --- |
| You are a victim of a crime | The contact should not affect your permit, but keep all confirmations |
| You have lost your permit card | Attach the police report to your application to Migri |
| Your permit has expired | If an extension application is filed late, the right of residence may be interrupted |
| An unclear letter or summons | Do not ignore it; seek an explanation |

Migri warns that if a permit application is filed late, the right of residence will be interrupted, and the police may fine a person for staying without a permit. Therefore, monitor the validity of your permit. We wrote about this in detail in articles on missing a Migri deadline.

## Common mistakes when contacting the police

Most mistakes stem from haste and an insufficient description of the event. These are the ones we see most often.

1. Calling 112 in non-emergency situations.
2. An overly general description of the event without time, place and details.
3. Lack of copies of documents and evidence.
4. Delay in reporting a loss or theft.
5. Failure to provide contact details, so the police cannot get in touch.
6. Providing false information or concealing important circumstances.

Many mistakes can be avoided if you prepare for the visit. Write down the chronology of events and gather all supporting evidence.

results.title: Migri requested additional documents: how to respond correctly
results.author: Anna Müller
highlights:
Sometimes documents cannot be obtained within the time allowed. In that case, it is important to act proactively rather than silently miss the deadline. Do not submit doubtful or forged documents. This will create far more serious problems than a short deadline. If you have doubts about the origin or accuracy of a document, first verify it with the authority that issued it, and only then add it to the response.

## Typical mistakes when responding to a Migri request

Below are the mistakes that occur most often. Each of them could have been avoided.

1. Missing the deadline or sending the response at the last moment
2. Responding to only part of the requirements and ignoring the rest
3. Submitting documents without an apostille or translation when these are required
4. Failing to explain the absence of a document
5. Failing to keep proof of submission
6. Relying on advice from forums instead of the text of the request

Each mistake may affect the decision. Missing the deadline and submitting an incomplete response are particularly risky. Therefore, before sending, compare your response once more with the text of the request and make sure that no requirement has been omitted and that all attachments are legible.

results.title: Moving to Finland – guide, checklists and address book
highlights:
### International or temporary protection

Asylum can only be applied for in person inside Finland, and since the EU Pact on Migration and Asylum applied on 12 June 2026 the deadlines are strict: register with the police or border authorities within 5 days and lodge the application with Migri (Finnish Immigration Service; Migrationsverket) within 21 days. Temporary protection for people fleeing Ukraine has been extended to 4 March 2028; current permits run to 4 March 2027 and Migri will extend them without a new card application.

| Step | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| Make the application in person | Apply at the border, the police or a Migri reception centre in Helsinki, Joutseno or Oulu – never by letter, email or at an embassy. Register within 5 days and lodge within 21 days (5 in the border procedure), or it may be deemed withdrawn. – Where: Migri (Finnish Immigration Service) |
| Temporary protection: apply free at the police | People from Ukraine apply free of charge at the police or a border authority after arrival; the decision takes about 2 weeks and the card 2 weeks more, with your henkilötunnus (personal identity code) printed on it. From 5 August 2026 you must show you were authorised to leave Ukraine. – Where: Migri (Finnish Immigration Service) |
| Start working | Asylum seekers may work after 3 months with a valid passport, 6 months without one, in any field. Temporary-protection holders may work in any sector immediately after applying and use municipal employment services once the permit is granted. – Where: Migri (Finnish Immigration Service) |
| Get a kotikunta when you qualify | Reception services end 3 months after a permit is granted – then apply to DVV for a kotikunta (municipality of residence). Temporary-protection holders can apply online after one year counted from the application date, with a permit valid at least a year. – Where: DVV (Digital and Population Data Services Agency) |
| Move from reception allowance to Kela | Temporary-protection holders get Kela (Social Insurance Institution) benefits after working or living in Finland for a year; before that the reception centre supports you. Refugees and subsidiary-protection holders are exempt from the permit income requirement. – Where: Kela (Social Insurance Institution) |
| Use health care | With a kotikunta you use the terveysasema (health station) of your hyvinvointialue (wellbeing services county); pending asylum seekers get care via the reception centre. National maximum doctor's fee €30.20 in 2026, counties may charge less – Helsinki €0. – Where: Your hyvinvointialue (wellbeing services county) |
| Renew in time | Asylum is granted for 3 years, subsidiary protection for 1 year, both with an unrestricted right to work – apply for an extension before expiry. Without a national passport you need a refugee travel document or an alien's passport. – Where: Migri (Finnish Immigration Service) |

| Rules that apply to you |
| --- |
| Since 16 June 2025 a sponsor with subsidiary protection, or a refugee with a new family, must have lived in Finland 2 years with a permit before family can apply; established refugee families and temporary-protection families are exempt. |
| A temporary-protection permit expires automatically if you are granted another permit on or after 12 June 2026; Migri recommends applying for an extended permit if you have a job or study place. |
| Temporary-protection holders and people granted asylum cannot get an EU Blue Card but can apply for a specialist permit; they are exempt from the €100 application fee and from tuition. |
| Permanent residence since 8 January 2026: 6 years on an A permit, 2 years' work and B1 Finnish or Swedish; no passport is needed with international protection, but a prison sentence resets the residence period. |
| After a legally valid negative decision reception services continue for at most 60 days; subsequent applicants get them for at most 14 days after the right of residence ends.

results.title: Seeking Asylum in Finland: How the Process Works (2026 Guide) | FinnAdvisor
highlights: The interview is the most important part of the process. Migri asks about who you are and why you need protection. Explain your reasons clearly and consistently, and bring any evidence you have. You can use an interpreter. Because how you present your case matters so much, advice before the interview is valuable — contact legal aid or an NGO early.
